# mysuite command reference

<!-- generated by `mysuite schema --markdown`; do not edit by hand -->

## Global options

- `--allow` - Sandbox: only read/write inside this folder (repeatable). Also set by MYSUITE_ROOTS. A path outside is refused with exit code 3. Meant for agents.
- `--sandbox` - Sandbox: allow only the current folder (same as --allow .).
- `--profile / -P` - Company profile from mysuite.toml ([profiles.NAME]): tokens, brand, variants, export defaults, metadata policy, allowed folders. Also MYSUITE_PROFILE. Flags still win.

## Exit codes

- `0` - ok
- `1` - at least one item failed (or an unexpected error)
- `2` - bad usage (unknown option, missing argument, a value not in `choices`) - from the CLI this is not JSON (it comes from the argument parser); MCP tools return it as JSON
- `3` - refused by the sandbox/policy - nothing was written
- `4` - a required external tool is missing - see missing_tools for install hints

## Item statuses (`items[].status`)

- `planned` - dry run: this would be written (nothing was)
- `written` - the output file was written
- `skipped_existing` - the output already exists and --overwrite was not given; nothing was written
- `skipped` - not done: a pipeline step after a failure, a dry-run step that can't preview, or a kit file that doesn't apply
- `failed` - this item failed; see `error`
- `missing` - doctor: this tool is not installed (see `required`, `unlocks` and `install_hint`)
- `ok` - a read-only result (inspect, contrast, diff, ocr, a pipeline step that ran)
- `warning` - inspect: the file was read, but something is wrong with it; see the item's `warnings`
- `done` - enhance: the picture was processed and written
- `group` - dupes: one group of identical or look-alike files
- `not_smaller` - pdf compress: the result would not be smaller, so nothing was written (no `output`)
- `marked` - mark detect: the mark was found
- `not_found` - mark detect: the mark was not found
- `installed` - install: the component was installed
- `already_installed` - install: nothing to do
- `removed` - install --remove: the component was deleted
- `not_installed` - install --remove: there was nothing to delete
- `invalid` - profiles list: this profile has an error
- `problem` - profiles check: this check failed
- `deleted` - profiles delete: the profile was removed
- `not_generated` - testcases: this sample needs a tool that is missing, so it was not made

## `mysuite compress`

Re-encode image(s) via a best-in-class codec (mozjpeg/webp/avif/oxipng/pngquant/gifsicle), with optional sharpening.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, repeatable) One or more files, and/or directories, to compress (non-recursive unless --recursive). Not needed with --list-presets.
- `--preset` (str) Named settings bundle (codec + its parameters) to start from — run --list-presets to see them. Any other flag you also pass overrides that field of the preset; --codec becomes optional when --preset is given.
- `--list-presets` (boolean) List available compress presets and exit.
- `--codec` (str) Target codec: mozjpeg, webp, avif, oxipng, pngquant, gifsicle. Required unless --preset supplies one.
- `--quality` (int range) Codec quality, 0-100 (mozjpeg/webp/avif only — ignored by oxipng/gifsicle, use --quality-range for pngquant).
- `--max-kb` (int range) Save for web: the file must be at most this many KB (1 KB = 1000 bytes). The highest quality that fits is searched for (mozjpeg/webp/avif); --quality, if given, is the highest it may use.
- `--max-size` (int range) Save for web: shrink so the longest side is at most this many pixels (never enlarges).
- `--sharpen-amount` (float) Unsharp mask amount applied before encoding (e.g. 1.0). Unset = no sharpening.
- `--sharpen-radius` (float) Unsharp mask radius (default 2.0).
- `--sharpen-sigma` (float) Unsharp mask sigma / blur amount (default 1.0).
- `--sharpen-threshold` (float) Unsharp mask threshold — minimum brightness change to sharpen (default 0.0).
- `--progressive / --baseline` (boolean) [mozjpeg] Progressive vs. baseline JPEG encoding (default progressive).
- `--subsample` (str) [mozjpeg] Chroma subsampling: 4:4:4 or 4:2:0 (default 4:2:0).
- `--lossless / --lossy` (boolean) [webp] Lossless encoding instead of lossy (default lossy).
- `--method` (int range) [webp] Compression effort, 0-6, slower = smaller (default 6).
- `--alpha-quality` (int range) [webp] Alpha channel quality, 0-100 (default 100).
- `--speed` (int range) [avif] Encoder speed, 0-10, slower = smaller (default 6).
- `--effort` (int range) [oxipng] Optimization effort, 0-6 (default 4).
- `--interlace / --no-interlace` (boolean) [oxipng] Apply Adam7 interlacing (default off).
- `--quality-range` (str) [pngquant] min-max quality range, e.g. 65-90 (default 65-90).
- `--pngquant-speed` (int range) [pngquant] Speed/quality trade-off, 1 (slow) - 11 (fast) (default 4).
- `--dither / --no-dither` (boolean) [pngquant] Floyd-Steinberg dithering (default on).
- `--optimize-level` (int range) [gifsicle] Optimization level, 1-3 (default 3).
- `--lossy` (int range) [gifsicle] Lossy compression amount, 0-200 (default 0).
- `--background` (str) Flatten transparency onto this colour (e.g. white, #ffffff). JPEG (mozjpeg) always flattens, on white unless you set this; other codecs keep transparency unless you set it.
- `--allow-larger` (boolean) Write the result even when it is larger than the original (by default nothing is written then).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories for folder inputs.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview input -> output pairs without compressing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite compress photo.jpg --codec mozjpeg --quality 80 --json
mysuite compress pics/ --codec webp --dry-run --json
```

## `mysuite contrast`

WCAG contrast ratio of two colours, or of a logo's colours on a background.

*read only · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `foreground` (str) Foreground colour, e.g. '#dd0000' (or use --logo).
- argument `background` (str) Background colour, e.g. white.
- `--logo` (file) Check every colour of this logo (SVG or image) against --on.
- `--on` (str, default `#ffffff`) Background for --logo (a colour or token:NAME).
- `--tokens` (str) Design token source (CSS/JSON file or folder, git+…, figma:…): then any colour may be token:NAME, e.g. token:--bg-color-brand-solid.
- `--brand` (str) Which brand of the token source (when it has several).
- `--theme` (choice, default `light`, one of `light`, `dark`) Which theme's token values to use.
- `--tokens-refresh` (boolean) Re-fetch a git token source.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite contrast "#dd0000" white --json
mysuite contrast --logo logo.svg --on "#ffffff" --json
mysuite contrast token:--text-color-brand token:--bg-color --tokens tokens/ --theme dark --json
```

## `mysuite convert`

Convert file(s) to another format, in place beside the source.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more files, and/or directories, to convert (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--to / -t` (str) Comma-separated target format(s), e.g. webp or png,pdf: bmp, eps, gif, ico, jpeg, pdf, png, tiff, webp (jpg and tif work too).
- `--quality` (int range) JPEG/WebP quality, 0-100.
- `--dpi / --ppi` (float, default `300`) Resolution used only when rasterizing a vector source (svg/pdf/eps); ignored for raster-to-raster conversions.
- `--background` (str) Flatten transparency onto a color (jpeg/bmp default to white if unset — they have no alpha channel).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories for folder inputs.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview input -> output pairs without converting.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite convert pic.png --to webp,jpeg --json
```

## `mysuite cutout`

Isolate a photo's subject into a transparent-background PNG (macOS Vision).

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more image files, and/or directories, to cut out (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories for folder inputs.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview input -> output pairs without cutting out anything.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite cutout photo.jpg --json
```

## `mysuite diff`

Compare two images: how much changed, optionally as a picture.

*read only unless `--out` (then writes files) · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `first` (file, required) Reference: an image, or an SVG/PDF/EPS (rendered; page 1).
- argument `second` (file, required) The image (or SVG/PDF/EPS) to compare.
- `--threshold` (int, default `16`) A pixel counts as changed when any channel differs by more than this (0-255).
- `--out / -o` (path) Write a PNG with the changed pixels in red over a faded first image.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite diff a.png b.png --json
mysuite diff old.svg new.svg --out changes.png --json
```

## `mysuite doctor`

Check the external tools: the required ones (rsvg-convert, gs, magick, exiftool) and the optional ones, with the commands each one unlocks. Exit 0 when every required tool is installed (optional ones may be missing).

*read only · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite doctor --json
```

## `mysuite dupes`

Find identical and look-alike images. Read only.

*read only · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Folders and/or images to compare.
- `--threshold` (int, default `5`) How different (bits of 64, 0-20) two pictures may be and still count as similar. 0 = look-alikes must hash identically.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite dupes photos/ --recursive --json
```

## `mysuite enhance history`

Show jobs recorded with --record-history.

*read only unless `--clear` (then writes files) · no `--dry-run`*

- `--limit` (int range, default `50`)
- `--clear` (boolean) Delete the history database.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite enhance history --limit 5
```

## `mysuite enhance presets`

List enhance presets (built-in and from mysuite.toml).

*read only · no `--dry-run`*

- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite enhance presets
```

## `mysuite enhance run`

Enhance photo(s), writing <name>_enhanced.<ext> beside each source.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more photos, and/or directories (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--preset` (str) Settings bundle to start from (see `mysuite enhance presets`). Any other flag you pass overrides that field. Default: gentle.
- `--scale` (int range) Upscale factor, 1-8.
- `--denoise` (float range) Denoise strength, 0-1.
- `--sharpen` (float range) Sharpen strength, 0-1.
- `--face-enhance / --no-face-enhance` (boolean) Face restoration (needs the optional AI backend).
- `--auto-white-balance / --no-auto-white-balance` (boolean) Gray-world white balance.
- `--saturation` (float range) 1.0 = unchanged.
- `--contrast` (float range) 1.0 = unchanged.
- `--gamma` (float range) 1.0 = unchanged, <1 brightens.
- `--restore-scratches / --no-restore-scratches` (boolean) Fill thin straight scratches/creases from their surroundings.
- `--format` (str) png, jpg or webp.
- `--quality` (int range) jpg/webp quality.
- `--backend` (str, default `auto`) auto, classical or realesrgan.
- `--record-history` (boolean) Log each job (paths, sizes, timing) to a local database for `enhance history`. Off by default: a log of what you processed is a trace.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing outputs.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) List input -> output pairs, write nothing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Print only the summary.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite enhance run photo.jpg --preset gentle --json
```

## `mysuite export`

Batch-export an SVG into multiple sizes, formats, and color profiles.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more SVG files (also .svgz, PDF, Illustrator .ai and EPS: converted to SVG first), and/or directories of SVGs (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--sizes / -s` (str) Comma-separated sizes: plain numbers are pixels, or suffix with mm/cm/in (e.g. 16,32,5cm,2in).
- `--formats / -f` (str) Comma-separated: png,pdf,eps,svg,jpeg,webp,tiff,ico,icns (ico/icns bundle multiple sizes into one file).
- `--vector-size` (str) Sizes the vector formats (svg, pdf, eps) are written at, once per variant and colour space: 'artwork' (default: the logo's own size, 1 px = 1 pt, no size in the file name) and/or sizes like 512 or 100mm, which fit like --sizes do (see --size-by). --sizes only sets the raster sizes.
- `--size-by` (choice) What each size sets: longest (default: the logo fits a SIZE x SIZE box), height or width. E.g. --sizes 512,1080 --size-by height makes a wide logo exactly 512 and 1080 px high.
- `--profiles / -p` (str) Comma-separated: rgb,cmyk
- `--dpi / --ppi` (float) Pixels/dots per inch used to convert mm/cm/in sizes to pixels (default from config, usually 300).
- `--unit` (choice) Default unit (px, mm, cm, or in) for sizes with no explicit suffix, e.g. --unit mm --sizes 50,80 means 50mm,80mm. Per-size suffixes still override this.
- `--background` (str) Background color (e.g. white, #ffffff) to flatten onto for formats without transparency. JPEG defaults to white if unset; other formats stay transparent.
- `--quality` (int range) JPEG/WebP compression quality (0-100).
- `--padding / --margin` (str) Uniform safe-space margin around the artwork for raster formats, e.g. 20, 20px, or 10%% of each size. No background color is forced — it stays transparent unless --background is also set. Vector formats (pdf/eps/svg) are unaffected. Overridden per side by --margin-top/-right/-bottom/-left.
- `--margin-top` (str) Top margin, overrides --margin for this side.
- `--margin-right` (str) Right margin, overrides --margin for this side.
- `--margin-bottom` (str) Bottom margin, overrides --margin for this side.
- `--margin-left` (str) Left margin, overrides --margin for this side.
- `--png-compression` (int range) PNG zlib compression level (0-9). Lossless either way — trades encode time for file size.
- `--out / -o` (path) Base output directory.
- `--name` (str) Override base name (default: each input file's stem). Only valid with a single input.
- `--naming` (str) File-name template, e.g. '{date}_BILD_Logo_{variant}_{size}_{COLORSPACE}{ext}'. Tokens: {name} {variant} {size} {size_px} {width} {height} (real pixels) {format} {colorspace} {ext} {date}; a token in CAPITALS gives a capitalised value. An empty token takes its separator with it (no variant: logo_512.png). Default: {name}_{variant}_{size}{ext}.
- `--path` (str) Folder template inside --out, ending in {naming} (the file name), e.g. '{COLORSPACE}/{FORMAT}/{naming}'. Same tokens as --naming. Default: {format}/{colorspace}/{naming} ({variant}/... first for a variant).
- `--name-folder / --no-name-folder` (boolean) Put each logo's files in a folder named after it (--out/<name>/..., the default); --no-name-folder writes the path template straight into --out.
- `--date-stamp / --no-date-stamp` (boolean) Insert today's date (YYYYMMDD) into filenames, e.g. logo_512_20260819.png. Only applies to the tool's own default naming templates — a naming_template you've already customized is left alone (it can reference {date} itself instead).
- `--variant` (str) Label this run as a variant (e.g. negative, mono) — nests output under exports/<name>/<variant>/... alongside the primary exports/<name>/... export instead of getting its own top-level name folder.
- `--recolor` (str, repeatable) Color substitution FROM=TO — hex (e.g. --recolor '#000000=#ffffff') or a named CSS color (e.g. --recolor 'white=black'). Repeatable, and each occurrence may itself hold several space/comma-separated pairs, e.g. --recolor '#000=#fff white=black'. TO may be 'transparent' (or 'none') to remove that colour, e.g. --recolor '#dd0000=transparent'. Applied to the SVG source before rendering.
- `--recolor-tolerance` (float range) How close (CIEDE2000 colour difference) a colour must be to a --recolor FROM to count as it; 0 = exact match only, 2 = just-noticeable difference (default 2, or the config's). Catches anti-aliased or slightly-off brand colours.
- `--cmyk-mode` (str) How CMYK numbers are chosen for --profiles cmyk (pdf/eps/tiff all use the same engine): 'exact' keeps the profile's values; 'clean' or 'clean:N' snaps every channel to a multiple of N (default 5, so 73/92 becomes 75/90) and prints the colour shift. Greys are always K-only.
- `--cmyk-profile` (file) CMYK ICC profile (e.g. FOGRA39 or your printer's) used for the conversion and embedded as the PDF output intent. Default: Ghostscript's SWOP profile.
- `--cmyk-map` (str, repeatable) Brand CMYK values, used as they are instead of computed: COLOUR=C/M/Y/K, e.g. '#DD0000=0/100/100/0'. Repeatable; one occurrence may hold several pairs. Matches the exact colour after --recolor and wins over --cmyk-mode (never rounded, greys not forced to K-only).
- `--tokens` (str) Design tokens: a .css/.json file or folder, git+https://host/org/repo@REF#path=dir (pinned, cached), or figma:FILEKEY. Lets --recolor use token:NAME and enables the negative variant.
- `--brand` (str) Which brand of the token source (when it has several).
- `--theme` (choice) Which theme's token values --recolor token:NAME uses: light (default) or dark.
- `--variants` (str) Several variants in one run, each in its own folder: default, negative (token-driven, needs --tokens), invert, mono-black, mono-white, grayscale, mono:COLOUR, knockout (shapes punched out of the background shape), cutout (background shape removed). Combine steps with + and name the folder with =, e.g. 'default,negativ_dark=knockout+mono:#1D1D1B,cut_out=cutout+mono-white'.
- `--negative-map` (str, repeatable) For the negative variant: LOGOCOLOUR=token:NAME makes that logo colour take the token's DARK value, e.g. '#1d1d1b=token:--headline-text-color'. Repeatable. Use it when several tokens share a colour but differ in dark mode.
- `--negative-tolerance` (float range, default `5.0`) How close (CIEDE2000) a logo colour must be to a token's light value for the negative variant to use that token.
- `--tokens-refresh` (boolean) Fetch a git token source again instead of using the cached copy.
- `--recursive` (boolean) When an input is a directory, include SVGs in subdirectories too.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--preset` (str) Name of a [presets.NAME] block to apply, or a built-in preset (favicon, macos-icon).
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview the output file tree without writing anything.
- `--strict` (boolean) Turn CMYK-unsupported-format warnings into hard errors.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--normalize-png / --no-normalize-png` (boolean) Tag PNG output with sRGB via ImageMagick.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite export logo.svg --formats png,pdf --sizes 64,512 --out dist --json
mysuite export logo.svg --formats pdf --profiles cmyk --cmyk-mode clean --sizes 100 --dry-run --json
mysuite export logo.svg --sizes 512,1080 --size-by height --json
```

## `mysuite inspect`

Report facts about image/vector files (size, colour mode, transparency, palette, sharpness, GPS...) - for agents and humans.

*read only unless `--thumb` / `--sheet` (then writes files) · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Files and/or folders to examine.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--thumb` (path) Write a <=512 px PNG preview of the (single) input, for clients that can look at images.
- `--sheet` (path) Write a labelled contact sheet PNG of all inputs.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite inspect logo.svg photo.jpg --json
mysuite inspect photo.jpg --thumb thumb.png --json
```

## `mysuite install`

Fetch the heavier parts once, when needed (helpers, the shield environment). mysuite itself stays small.

*read only unless `--yes` (then writes files) · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `name` (choice, one of `tools`, `cutout`, `vision`, `shield`) Component to install (see the list). Leave out to list them.
- `--yes / -y` (boolean) Go ahead without asking (required when there is no terminal, and with --json).
- `--remove` (boolean) Delete the component again.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Show what would be fetched/built and where, change nothing.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite install --json
mysuite install vision --dry-run --json
```

## `mysuite kit list`

List the available kits and what each one makes.

*read only · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite kit list --json
```

## `mysuite kit make`

Make a kit from a logo: `mysuite kit make logo.svg --kit favicon`.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Logo file(s): SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF, EPS…
- `--kit / -k` (str) Which kit: favicon, ios-app-icon, android-icons, social, retina. See `mysuite kit list`.
- `--out / -o` (path, default `kits`) Output folder. Files go to <out>/<logo name>/<kit>/…
- `--name` (str) Name used in the folder and file names (default: the logo's file name).
- `--background` (str) Colour behind the logo (e.g. '#ffffff'). Needed for social images; opaque icons default to white.
- `--padding` (float) Empty border around the logo, percent of the canvas (0-49).
- `--size` (int, default `64`) Retina kit only: the @1x size in pixels (@2x and @3x follow).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) List the files that would be written.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Print only the summary.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite kit make logo.svg --kit favicon --out kits --json
```

## `mysuite mark detect`

Check whether pictures carry YOUR mark. Exit code 1 if none of them does with --strict.

*read only · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Pictures to check.
- `--key` (str) Your secret key (or MYSUITE_MARK_KEY).
- `--id` (str) The id used when embedding (if any).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--strict` (boolean) Exit 1 when a picture does NOT carry the mark.
- `--deep` (boolean) Also look for slightly rotated copies (±3°): much slower.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite mark detect suspect.jpg --key SECRET --json
```

## `mysuite mark embed`

Add your invisible mark. Output: <name>_marked.png beside the original.

*writes files · no `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Images / folders.
- `--key` (str) Your secret key (or MYSUITE_MARK_KEY). Same key = same mark.
- `--id` (str) Optional label mixed into the mark, e.g. a campaign or recipient: a different id is a different mark.
- `--strength` (str, default `standard`) subtle (~44 dB), standard (~40 dB), strong (~37 dB): stronger survives more, shows more.
- `--format` (str, default `png`) png (best), tiff or jpeg.
- `--quality` (int, default `95`) JPEG quality.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite mark embed photo.png --key SECRET --json
```

## `mysuite mcp`

Run the MCP server (stdio) so MCP clients can use mysuite. Needs `pip install 'mysuite[mcp]'`. Sandboxed to --allow folders (default: the current folder).

*read only · no `--dry-run`*

- `--allow` (path, repeatable) Folder the server may read/write (repeatable). Default: the current folder.
- `--slim` (boolean) One short line per tool description, for small local models with little context (mysuite_schema has the detail).

Examples:

```bash
mysuite mcp --allow ~/Pictures/work
mysuite mcp --allow ~/Pictures/work --slim
```

## `mysuite metadata apply`

Apply a metadata policy in one go - the active profile's, or --policy: any of strip, randomize, credit, in order (e.g. strip,credit removes everything, then embeds your credit). Each step works on the previous step's output.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Image files and/or folders.
- `--policy` (str) Comma-separated steps: strip, randomize, credit (default: the profile's metadata.policy).
- `--author / -a` (str) For the credit step (default: the profile's metadata.author).
- `--copyright` (str) For the credit step (default: the profile's metadata.copyright).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview the final file names, write nothing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean)
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite metadata apply photo.jpg --policy strip,credit --author Acme --json
```

## `mysuite metadata credit`

Embed a signed C2PA provenance manifest (author/copyright) for correct crediting.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more image files, and/or directories (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--author / -a` (str) Author/creator name to embed (or the active profile's metadata.author).
- `--copyright` (str) Copyright notice to embed, e.g. '© 2026 Jane Doe'.
- `--no-ai` (boolean) Also record in the manifest that AI training, generative training, inference and data mining are NOT allowed (C2PA training-mining assertion).
- `--generator` (str, default `mysuite`) Software/tool named as the claim generator (not independently visible in c2patool's own read-back report on all versions — author/copyright are the fields that reliably read back).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview input -> output pairs, write nothing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite metadata credit photo.jpg --author "Name" --copyright "© 2026 Name" --json
```

## `mysuite metadata declare`

Write a machine-readable 'no AI use' declaration (PLUS DataMining + XMP Rights) into a copy (name_declared.ext). It is a legal/consent signal that cooperating crawlers and tools read - it does not technically block anything.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Image files and/or folders.
- `--policy` (str, default `prohibited`) prohibited, prohibited-ai-training, prohibited-genai-training: what is not allowed.
- `--owner` (str) Copyright owner name to record.
- `--terms-url` (str) Link to your AI-use terms.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--dry-run` (boolean)
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean)
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite metadata declare photo.jpg --owner Acme --json
```

## `mysuite pipeline run`

Run a pipeline file (TOML or JSON). Steps run in order; each takes the previous step's outputs.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `file` (file, required) Pipeline file (.toml or .json).
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Validate everything and show the plan; nothing is written. Step 1 is planned exactly; later steps that consume earlier outputs are listed symbolically (their file names exist only after the run). Read-only steps (inspect, dupes, contrast, pdf info…) really run. A step that could write files and has no --dry-run of its own is not run at all (status skipped, with a warning).
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml, passed to every step.
- `--keep-intermediate` (boolean) Keep the files earlier steps wrote and later steps replaced (by default they are deleted after a successful run; the file's `keep_intermediate = true` does the same). Files that already existed are never deleted.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite pipeline run release.toml --dry-run --json
mysuite pipeline run release.toml --json
```

## `mysuite preset save`

Save export settings as a new (or replacement) preset in mysuite.toml.

*writes files · no `--dry-run`*

- argument `name` (str, required) Preset name.
- `--sizes / -s` (str) Comma-separated sizes, e.g. 16,32,5cm,2in.
- `--formats / -f` (str) Comma-separated formats.
- `--profiles / -p` (str) Comma-separated: rgb,cmyk.
- `--dpi / --ppi` (float) Pixels/dots per inch.
- `--unit` (str) Default unit for bare sizes: px, mm, cm, in.
- `--background` (str) Background color.
- `--quality` (int range) JPEG/WebP quality.
- `--padding / --margin` (str) Uniform margin baseline, e.g. 20px or 10%%.
- `--margin-top` (str) Top margin override.
- `--margin-right` (str) Right margin override.
- `--margin-bottom` (str) Bottom margin override.
- `--margin-left` (str) Left margin override.
- `--png-compression` (int range) PNG compression level.
- `--out / -o` (str) Base output directory.
- `--date-stamp / --no-date-stamp` (boolean) Insert today's date into filenames.
- `--variant` (str) Variant label, e.g. negative, mono.
- `--recolor` (str, repeatable) Exact hex color substitution FROM=TO. Repeatable.
- `--strict / --no-strict` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--normalize-png / --no-normalize-png` (boolean)
- `--config / -c` (path) TOML file to save into (default: ./mysuite.toml).

Examples:

```bash
mysuite preset save web --formats png,webp --sizes 64,512
```

## `mysuite print`

Output at an exact size (10x15cm @300dpi = 1181x1772 px), dpi stored in the file.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Images (or SVG/PDF/EPS) to output at an exact size.
- `--size` (str) Exact output size: 10x15cm, 4x6in, 210x297mm or 1200x630px (plain numbers are pixels).
- `--dpi` (float, default `300.0`) Resolution for physical sizes, and the dpi written into the file.
- `--fit` (str, default `contain`) contain = whole picture inside (padded); cover = fill the size and crop; stretch = distort to fit.
- `--background` (str) Padding colour for contain (default transparent; white for JPEG).
- `--gravity` (str, default `center`) Where the picture sits (contain) or which part is kept (cover).
- `--bleed` (float) Print bleed in mm added around the size (0-50).
- `--auto-rotate` (boolean) Turn the picture 90° when its orientation doesn't match the paper.
- `--format` (str) png, jpeg, tiff or webp (default: same as the source).
- `--quality` (int, default `95`) JPEG quality 1-100.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Show the pixel size that would be written.
- `--config / -c` (path)
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite print photo.jpg --size 10x15cm --dpi 300 --fit cover --json
mysuite print pic.png --size 1200x630 --fit cover --json
```

- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)

```bash
mysuite profile photo.tif --to cmyk --cmyk-mode clean --json
```

## `mysuite profiles save`

Create or replace a profile in mysuite.toml. Only the options you give are stored.

- `--brand` (str)
- `--theme` (str) light or dark.
- `--variants` (str) Default logo variants, e.g. default,negative.
- `--negative-map` (str, repeatable) LOGOCOLOUR=token:NAME (repeatable).
- `--allow` (str, repeatable) Sandbox folder(s) this profile may read/write (repeatable).
- `--formats` (str) Export formats, comma-separated.
- `--sizes` (str) Export sizes, comma-separated.

- `--cmyk-mode` (str) exact, clean or clean:N.

- `--out-dir` (str) Export output folder.
- `--background` (str)
- `--policy` (str) Metadata policy steps, e.g. strip,credit.
- `--author` (str) Metadata credit: author.
- `--copyright` (str) Metadata credit: copyright line.
- `--no-ai / --allow-ai` (boolean) Metadata: record a 'no AI training/mining' declaration.
- `--terms-url` (str) Metadata declare: link to your AI-use terms.
- `--compress-preset` (str)
- `--enhance-preset` (str)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Replace a profile of the same name.


## `mysuite relight`

Experimental: re-shade a picture as if lit from another direction (classical, no AI model).

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Photos/images to relight (raster formats).
- `--preset` (str) Lighting preset: key-left, key-right, top, side, dramatic, golden-hour, cool-fill. Other flags override it.
- `--direction` (str) Where the light comes from: top, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, left, top-left. Default top-left.
- `--angle` (float) Compass degrees the light comes FROM (0 top, 90 right, 180 bottom, 270 left); beats --direction.
- `--height` (float) Light elevation in degrees, 1-90 (90 = straight on, low = raking). Default 40.
- `--intensity` (float) How strongly the light shapes the picture, 0-3. Default 0.9.
- `--ambient` (float) Base light everywhere, 0-2 (lower = deeper shadows). Default 0.55.
- `--softness` (float) Blur of the shape in percent of the short side, 0-50. Default 6.
- `--depth` (float) How pronounced the pseudo-3D is, 0-5. Default 1.
- `--specular` (float) Sheen, 0 = matte. Default 0.
- `--color` (str) Tint of the light, e.g. '#ffb36b' (warm) or '#9ec5ff' (cool).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing outputs.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) List input -> output pairs, write nothing.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Print only the summary.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite relight product.png --preset golden-hour --json
```

## `mysuite rename`

Rename many files by a pattern ({n}, {date}, {name}...). Copies by default.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Files and/or folders to rename.
- `--pattern` (str) New name with tokens: {name} {ext} {n} {n:3} {date} {datetime} {w} {h}, e.g. 'trip_{n:3}{ext}'.
- `--start` (int, default `1`) Number of the first file ({n}).
- `--sort` (str, default `name`) Order for {n}: name, date (EXIF capture time, else file time) or size.
- `--out / -o` (path) Folder for the renamed COPIES (default: beside the originals).
- `--move` (boolean) Rename the originals in place instead of making renamed copies.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean)
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean)
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Show the old -> new names, change nothing.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite rename photos/ --pattern "trip_{n:3}{ext}" --dry-run --json
```

EXPERIMENTAL: make images resist AI image editing (PhotoGuard-style). Needs `mysuite install shield`.

## `mysuite svg optimise`

Make SVGs smaller without changing how they look: no editor leftovers, tidy colours, rounded numbers. Checked by rendering both versions.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) SVG / .svgz files and/or folders.
- `--precision` (int range, default `3`) Decimals kept in coordinates (3 is invisible at normal sizes; small viewBoxes automatically keep 2 more).
- `--keep-ids` (boolean) Keep every id (needed if scripts or other files point into the SVG).
- `--remove-title` (boolean) Also drop <title> and <desc> (they help screen readers).
- `--verify / --no-verify` (boolean, default `True`) Render before and after and refuse to write a file that looks different.
- `--svgz` (boolean) Write gzip-compressed .svgz instead of .svg.
- `--out / -o` (path) Output folder (default: beside each source, as <name>.min.svg).
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Report the savings, write nothing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Print only the summary.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite svg optimise logo.svg --json
```

## `mysuite transform`

Quick edits: trim, crop, rotate, flip, resize, pad, round corners, background (fixed, predictable order).

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) Files and/or folders to edit.
- `--trim` (boolean) Cut away a uniform border (transparent, else the top-left colour).
- `--trim-fuzz` (float range) How much a pixel may differ from the border colour, in percent.
- `--crop` (str) Crop box WIDTHxHEIGHT+X+Y in pixels, e.g. 800x600+100+50.
- `--crop-aspect` (str) Crop to an aspect ratio like 16:9 or 1:1, keeping as much as possible (see --gravity).
- `--gravity` (str, default `center`) Which part to keep/anchor: center, top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
- `--rotate` (float) Rotate clockwise by this many degrees (90/180/270 are exact).
- `--flip` (str) Mirror: horizontal, vertical or both.
- `--resize` (str) 512 (width), x512 (height), 512x512 (box) or 50%. See --resize-mode.
- `--resize-mode` (str, default `fit`) fit = inside the box keeping aspect; fill = cover the box and crop; exact = stretch.
- `--shrink-only` (boolean) Never enlarge: leave images already smaller than the target alone.
- `--pad` (str) Extend the canvas to an aspect (1:1) or size (1200x630) without cropping.
- `--pad-color` (str) Padding colour (default transparent; white for JPEG).
- `--round` (str) Round the corners: radius in px (24) or percent (50% on a square = circle).
- `--background` (str) Flatten transparency onto this colour.
- `--format` (str) png, jpeg, webp or tiff (default: same as the source; vectors become PNG).
- `--quality` (int range) JPEG/WebP quality.
- `--suffix` (str, default `_transformed`) Added to the file name; the original is never modified.
- `--no-auto-orient` (boolean) Do not apply the EXIF rotation first.
- `--dpi` (float, default `300.0`) Rasterisation density for SVG/PDF/EPS sources.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing outputs.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) List input -> output pairs, write nothing.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Print only the summary.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite transform pic.png --crop-aspect 1:1 --resize 512 --round 50% --json
```

## `mysuite watermark`

Stamp a logo onto image(s) as a visible, scalable watermark.

*writes files · has `--dry-run` · `--json`*

- argument `inputs` (path, required, repeatable) One or more image files, and/or directories, to watermark (non-recursive unless --recursive).
- `--logo / -l` (path) Image (or SVG) to stamp onto each input as the watermark.
- `--position / -p` (str, default `bottom-right`) One of: top-left, top-center, top-right, center-left, center, center-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right.
- `--scale` (float, default `15.0`) Logo width as a percentage of the base image's width.
- `--opacity` (int range, default `80`) Watermark blend opacity, 0-100.
- `--margin` (float, default `3.0`) Breathing room from the edge, as a percentage of the base image's width.
- `--recursive / -r` (boolean) Recurse into subdirectories for folder inputs.
- `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` (boolean) Overwrite existing output files.
- `--dry-run` (boolean) Preview input -> output pairs without watermarking anything.
- `--config / -c` (path) Explicit path to mysuite.toml.
- `--quiet / -q` (boolean) Suppress per-file progress, print summary only.
- `--json` (boolean) Print one machine-readable JSON document on stdout (human text goes to stderr). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 some item failed, 2 bad usage, 3 refused by policy, 4 missing tool.

Examples:

```bash
mysuite watermark photo.jpg --logo logo.svg --position bottom-right --json
```
